intro: Professionals and everyday users convert radians (rad) to degrees (°) when working across si and other standards in CNC rotary indexing, optical alignment, trigonometric engineering, and surveying bearings. One radian equals 57.29578 degrees, while 1 degree equals 0.017453 radians. Whether you are verifying angle specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Radian to Degree is 57.29577951, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many degrees (°) are in 1 radian (rad)?
faqs.answer: There are 57.29577951 degrees (°) in 1 radian (rad), which rounds to 57.2958 ° for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 degree equals 0.017453 radians.

faqs.question: How do I convert radians to degrees (rad to °)?
faqs.answer: To convert radians to degrees, use the formula: ° = rad × 57.29577951. For example, converting 90 rad gives 5,156.6202 °.

faqs.question: What is 90 radians in degrees?
faqs.answer: 90 radians (rad) equals exactly 5,156.6202 degrees (°) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
